jobs.title: Principal HR Business Partner - Tech
jobs.description:
Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve.

Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals.

About The Role

As Hims & Hers continues to scale, the complexity of our business, leaders, and organization continues to grow. We're looking for a Principal HR Business Partner to help shape what's next.

This is a highly strategic role that requires exceptional business acumen as much as HR expertise. The right person will develop a deep understanding of our business, operating model, and leadership priorities, then translate that understanding into building organizations, leadership teams, and talent strategies that enable the business to move faster and scale effectively.

You'll serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, helping shape not only organizational decisions, but how leaders think about organization, leadership, and talent. You'll bring an independent point of view, challenge assumptions, connect patterns others don't see, and help leaders navigate the moments that matter most.

This role is equally about solving today's challenges and building the organizational capability needed for tomorrow. Success isn't defined by the number of decisions you support. It's defined by the quality of the organizations, leaders, and operating models you help build.

You Will

Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, helping shape business strategy through organization design, leadership, and talent.
Lead organization design, workforce planning, and succession efforts that position the business for its next stage of growth.
Partner with leaders to design organizations that create clear ownership, accelerate decision making, and enable teams to scale.
Coach senior leaders through organizational change, leadership transitions, performance challenges, and other high-impact business moments.
Bring a clear, well-reasoned point of view to complex organizational decisions, helping leaders evaluate tradeoffs and move forward with confidence.
Identify emerging organizational risks and opportunities by connecting themes across leaders, teams, and the broader business before they become barriers to execution.
Build practical, scalable approaches that improve how leaders lead, how teams operate, and how the organization grows over time.
Partner closely with Recruiting, Compensation, Employment Legal, HR Operations, and other People leaders to ensure business decisions are supported with thoughtful, integrated People strategies.
Raise the standard for HR partnership by modeling exceptional business thinking, organizational insight, and leadership influence while helping develop other HRBPs across the team.
Master, own, and interpret People programs (e.g., Compensation, Legal, Performance) to provide authoritative guidance to the business, knowing that strategic partnership at this level is built on a foundation of operational excellence.

You Have

12+ years of progressive HR experience, including senior HRBP partnership in operational or complex environments
Significant experience partnering with senior business leaders in complex, high-growth organizations.
Demonstrated success leading organization design, workforce planning, leadership development, and talent strategy.
Strong business acumen with the ability to translate complex business challenges into practical organizational solutions.
Proven ability to influence executive leaders through credibility, thoughtful challenge, and a clear point of view.
Experience helping organizations navigate growth, transformation, and organizational change.
Demonstrated ability to anticipate organizational issues, connect patterns across the business, and proactively solve problems before they slow the organization down.
Strong executive presence with the confidence to coach leaders, challenge assumptions, and influence important business decisions.
A builder's mindset with a track record of creating scalable approaches that improve how organizations operate over time.
Ability to move seamlessly between long-term strategy and hands-on execution in a fast-paced environment.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

We're committed to building a team that reflects diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe different ways of thinking make us stronger, and we're dedicated to creating an environment where everyone feels valued, supported, and empowered to do their best work.

If you're excited about this opportunity, we encourage you to apply—even if your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification. We know that great candidates often bring transferable skills and unique perspectives that don't fit neatly into a checklist.

Hims & Hers is an equal opportunity employer. We make employment decisions based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without discrimination on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law.

If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know. We're committed to providing an inclusive and accessible experience for all candidates.

jobs.description:
About SandboxAQ

SandboxAQ is a high-growth company delivering AI solutions that address some of the world's greatest challenges. The company’s Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) power advances in life sciences, financial services, navigation, cybersecurity, and other sectors.

We are a global team that is tech-focused and includes experts in AI, chemistry, cybersecurity, physics, mathematics, medicine, engineering, and other specialties. The company emerged from Alphabet Inc. as an independent, growth capital-backed company in 2022, funded by leading investors and supported by a braintrust of industry leaders.

At SandboxAQ, we’ve cultivated an environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and impact. By investing deeply in our people, we’re building a thriving, global workforce poised to tackle the world's epic challenges. Join us to advance your career in pursuit of an inspiring mission, in a community of like-minded people who value entrepreneurialism, ownership, and transformative impact.

The Opportunity

At SandboxAQ, People infrastructure is not a back-office function. It is the platform on which we build the employee experience.

We have strong foundations in place, and we are entering the next evolution of how we operate. As the company grows, we need someone who can build for today while designing for what comes next. What works at 300 people is not what works at 600, and this role is about helping us stay ahead of that curve.

We are looking for a HR Operations Lead to own and evolve our People Infrastructure in North America, with select global overlap. This is a senior role that is both hands on, as well as responsible for the work and execution of more junior team members. The right person will bring strong judgment, systems thinking, and a practical builder mindset. They will know how to create infrastructure and experiences that work for employees, managers, and the business at the same time.

This person will lead across systems, workflows, policy, service delivery, and operational design. They should be comfortable being hands on and running critical day-to-day operations, improving the architecture behind them, and bringing practical ideas (that you have implemented prior!) for how AI and agentic workflows can help us work smarter as we scale. Experience supporting organizational growth, change, and M&A integration is highly valuable in this role.

Key Responsibilities

Own HR Operations for North America across the employee lifecycle, while partnering on selected global processes and initiatives.
Lead operational excellence across employee changes, leaves, separations, compliance, documentation, and employee support.
Own and improve core HR systems, workflows, and operating infrastructure with a focus on scale, usability, control, and reliability.
Translate policy into clear, workable processes and build durable operating practices, documentation, and governance.
Strengthen workflows for contractors, consultants, advisors, and other non-employee populations.
Manage and develop junior HR Operations team members, creating clarity, accountability, and stronger execution across the team.
Partner closely with the People Team, Talent Acquisition, Finance, Legal, IT, Security, and other stakeholders to improve how work moves across the business.
Identify friction, reduce manual work, and introduce practical uses of AI, automation, and agentic workflows to improve quality, speed, and scale.
Help the function evolve for the future by building infrastructure that can support a more complex organization over time, including periods of rapid growth, change, or integration.
Lead on select sensitive employee relations matters including investigations, policy review, and decision making
Drive strategic projects and programs to make us more future ready (ex: roadmap for tech stack changes, new global time off policies)

Essential Skills & Experience

Significant experience in HR Operations, People Operations, or HR systems-focused roles, with ownership of regional or multi-jurisdictional operations. Prior deliverables may include (but not limited to):
Technology evaluation, re-design and implementation (ex: new HRIS system)
Significant policy design and transition (ex: you made a large scale global policy change and drove the change management)
Redesigning work flows with the use of AI/agentic solutions
Experience leading complex employee relations matters (ex: difficult policy decision, standard employee investigation)

Minimum of 9+ years of progressive experience across HR systems, operational infrastructure, employee lifecycle processes, policy execution, and service delivery.
Someone who has held an HR Business Partner role (or similar employee facing role)
Prior people management experience, including meaningful experience coaching and developing junior team members.
Strong systems orientation and comfort with HRIS platforms, workflow tools, reporting, and process design.
Experience building or maturing contractor, consultant, or non-employee workforce processes.
Experience supporting company growth and change, with exposure to M&A, integration, or organizational transition work strongly preferred.
Ability to think beyond the current moment and design for where the company is going, not just where it is today.
Strong judgment, high discretion, and the ability to move fluidly between strategy and hands-on execution.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to turn ambiguity into clear action.
Experience in an AI-focused, high-growth, or highly innovative environment, with credible ideas for how AI and agentic approaches can level up HR Operations.

Highly Desired Skills & Experience

You are curious, highly responsive, and energized by building better ways of working.
You bring both creativity and pragmatism, and know how to balance fresh thinking with what will actually work.
You can see both the immediate operational need and the longer-term operating model behind it.
You care about quality and discipline, but you are not attached to process for process’s sake.
You like using technology to modernize work and improve the employee experience.
You know how to lead others while staying close enough to the details to keep the function sharp.
You want to be ahead of the competition versus waiting to see if what others are doing will work.
You are highly collaborative, stakeholder oriented, and communicative.

Why Join Us?

We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and life outside of work.

Career Defining Work: Your work will directly accelerate the discovery of better drugs and better materials, advance human health, and enable safer and more sustainable technologies by helping customers put AI Simulation capabilities into real world use.
Compensation: Competitive base salary, performance-based incentives or bonuses (where applicable), and equity participation.
Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents with generous employer premium contributions, retirement savings with company matching, paid parental leave, and inclusive family-building benefits.
Work-Life Balance: Fully remote, Flexible paid time off, company-wide seasonal breaks, and support for flexible work arrangements that enable sustainable performance.
Learning and Growth: Opportunities for continuous learning and growth through on-the-job development, cross-functional collaboration, and access to internal learning and development programs.

Strong understanding of employee relations and performance management.
Excellent communication and coaching skills.

Maximize productivity by eliminating inefficiency

Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

We're hiring a People Operations Manager to own our People data and the reporting built on top of it, alongside a slice of the operational work that generates it.

Cohere is scaling fast and leadership needs numbers they can trust. Today those numbers take too long to produce and they don't always agree with each other. Reporting is only as good as the data underneath it, which is why this role runs real processes as well as reporting on them.

This is a hands-on building role. You will own headcount, attrition and cost reporting, define what our metrics actually mean, and own benefits administration and employee records end to end. You will own the answer, not just the spreadsheet. A useful lens; this role means nobody has to debate whose number is right.

You'll join a small HR Operations team during our Rippling implementation, which means greenfield opportunity and real influence over how our data is structured for the next few years.

What You'll Do

Own the numbers

Own headcount, attrition and people cost reporting end to end
Build the exec and board level reporting our leadership relies on
Define what our metrics mean, rather than producing whatever is asked for

Fix the data underneath

Reconcile People and Finance headcount, and keep them reconciled
Clean up the taxonomies that make reporting unreliable, starting with termination reasons
Chase the data quality problems nobody has asked you to chase
Build the checks that stop bad data entering in the first place

Own the data model

Own our employee data model, definitions and governance
Work with the HRIS team so the system supports the reporting we need
Push and challenge current systems to meet your data vision

Own Benefits Administration And Records

Own US and global benefits administration, renewal cycles and open enrolment
Own employee records, employment verification and data requests
Support the front line team who handle day to day employee questions

Make reporting self-serve

Automate the recurring reporting so it produces itself
Give managers and leaders access to their own numbers
Reduce the number of requests that need a person at all

Build For What's Coming

Produce reporting that stands up to audit and external diligence
Work with Finance and IT on the controls and evidence our data needs to carry
Design for a company several times our current size

Manage a team

Led and developed a high-performing team through regular coaching, feedback, and performance management while maintaining team cohesion and morale
Managed day-to-day operations and resource allocation for a small team, balancing project priorities, resolving conflicts, and ensuring timely delivery of deliverables within budget constraints

5+ years of people analytics and reporting experience, within fast-paced, scaling environments
Meaningful experience delivering people operations solutions across all aspects of the talent journey
Experienced in HRIS implementation or migration
Experience building reports from scratch
Proactively identify and resolve data quality issues, maintaining high standards for clean, reliable analytics data
Effectively communicate data insights by explaining numerical findings, their source methodology, and rationale for discrepancies with alternative interpretations
Write clearly and document by default
Have run operations across multiple countries and entities, including EOR or contractor populations
Are comfortable anywhere across the employee journey, from hire to exit
Pick up new tools quickly and become the person others ask
Enjoy building elegant solutions to messy operational problems

Bonus if you have

Worked in Rippling, or implemented it
People management experience
Built reporting in a BI tool, or worked comfortably in SQL
Been in a company through IPO readiness or SOC 2 and SOX preparation

Someone who waits for a report request and fills it. This role decides what we measure and makes the underlying data good enough to trust. If you would rather be handed a spec than write one, this is not the role for you.

About Edra

Edra is solving one of the hardest problems in enterprise AI: AI models are generic but company processes are specific. We build AI agents that learn how processes actually run, and then run their operations.

We're a Series A startup, backed by Sequoia and other leading VC firms, led by Co-Founders who created and led Forward Deployed AI Engineering at Palantir, and we're growing our team in New York and London. We're a deeply technical team of engineers, AI researchers, and strategists with a high bar for talent and a shared belief that exceptional people are the foundation of everything great we'll build.

The Role

Edra is 30+ people across New York and London, with aggressive hiring plans in both offices. Every one of those people runs through an offer, payroll in one of two countries, equity in one of two tax regimes, benefits, and the compliance layer underneath it all. We've laid the foundation; now we want someone to own it, and to build the version that gets us to 60, 100, and beyond.

You'll own the employee lifecycle end to end in both countries: US and UK payroll, benefits in both regimes, onboarding, and people compliance across two jurisdictions. At most companies, people ops is carved into slices; here you own the whole stack, with real autonomy to determine how it runs. You'll own these systems internally, working directly with our payroll providers, benefits brokers, accountants, and employment counsel where specialist expertise is needed.

That's the exciting part, so we'll be specific about it: this is a builder and operator role. You'll inherit working processes and be expected to replace each one as we outgrow it: automating what's manual, rebuilding for scale, and designing the systems a much larger Edra will still be running down the line. And because we're an AI company, we expect you to build like one. Edra's platform is available to you as a tool for your own function, and we want you using it (along with everything else in a modern AI startup stack) to build and run a people operation that's leaner, faster, and more precise than a traditional people operation. If you've ever looked at a payroll reconciliation or an onboarding checklist and thought “a system should be doing this!” this is the place to prove it.

One thing to be upfront about: comp philosophy, equity strategy, and performance management remain Founder-owned. You'll make those programs operationally excellent: the data, tooling, process, communication, and execution behind them.

What You'll Do

Be the first point of contact for operational people questions (payroll, benefits, leave, equity administration, and employment logistics) and resolve them quickly and clearly.
Own US and UK payroll end to end: run it, reconcile it, handle joiners and leavers, catch problems before they reach a paycheck, and fix the ones that do fast.
Design and build our onboarding program from first principles, so new hires are set up to take ownership and have impact from day one, in either office.
Automate onboarding and offboarding processes across both entities: equipment and access provisioning, benefits enrollment, compliance training, and more.
Administer benefits in both countries: US healthcare and 401(k), including open enrollment and renewals; UK pension and benefits.
Own the operational compliance calendar across both countries, including required payroll, benefits, employment, and personnel processes and filings.
Keep Rippling accurate as the source of record for headcount, comp, and org data, and extend it wherever it can take work off a human
Build automations and internal tooling for repetitive people workflows, using Edra’s own platform and other AI tools wherever they can improve speed, accuracy, or employee experience.

What We’re Looking For

You've owned significant parts of people operations at a startup through a growth phase. You've personally processed payroll, fixed benefits enrollment errors, and onboarded new team members, not just managed vendors who did.
You've worked across US and UK employment infrastructure, or have international people ops experience and can close the gap quickly.
You default to systems. When something breaks twice, you fix the process, and when a task is repetitive, you automate it rather than staffing it.
You're curious about what AI tooling can do for an operations function, and you'd rather experiment and find out than wait for a vendor to tell you.
You're detail-oriented at the level this work requires. Errors in payroll and benefits are visible to everyone—you make sure they don’t happen.
You write clearly, especially when explaining equity, benefits, and policy to people who aren't specialists.
You handle confidential comp and performance information with discretion.

UK payroll and pensions depth
Experience standing up new benefits programs in the US and UK
Fluency with Rippling
Track record of building automation or tooling inside an ops function
